items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: And old man, Conchal, was working at Rice. That's right, I used to replace him.

ctx.x: And when did the piano come into the line?

Well, the piano, well, I'll tell you about the piano. When they put a piano in the band, I mean, I couldn't get what the piano. You know, so used to playing just the bass and the guitar, you know, it was so nice, you know. I wasn't used to putting custom to it, you know what I mean? And I said, oh, this don't make sense, I mean, because we never had no piano in the band, you know. Pianos always played alone by themselves, you know. I remember the district, all the guys, you know, played mostly alone, you know.…
Would the piano be on the right or the left, though? How would it vary?

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: I relief old man Contrell at Rice. I used to relief him there.

ctx.x: They always do it the same way. They used to.

That's right. Right. That's right. You hit the first note on the right foot? Yeah, right on the right foot, yeah. What places did you play in the district? Oh, in the district? Let me see. I worked at, I didn't work regular. I mean I, I relief old man Contrell at Rice. I used to relief him there. And then I relief Henry Zeno at Pete Lala. I used to relief him there. When King Oliver had the band, Joe Oliver had the band. He wasn't King then. It was Joe, Joe Oliver. And then I played at Few Clothes a few times.…
